text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: euc1c ALB error-rate spike detected. 5xx rate > 12% over 1m for service=ingress-api, targetgroup=ingress-pool-euc1c. Auto-escalation to on-call.
emily.g: Acknowledged, I'm on it. Pulling LB metrics and recent deploys.
raj.s: I see a simultaneous rise in TCP resets from Envoy in that AZ. Possible backend connection saturation. Tagging @maria_ops for customer-impact.
maria_ops: Noted — checking customer dashboards for erroring tenants now.
zach_infra: I'm looking at NLB health checks and backend EC2 metrics. CPU and connection count look normal on hosts in euc1c, but envoy workers show backlog.
emily.g: Running a quick tail on envoy logs for ingress pods in euc1c:
```
kubectl -n ingress-prod logs -l app=envoy -c proxy --since=2m | grep "reset" | tail -n 20
2026-03-15T12:01:23Z envoy proxy reset stream: downstream connection reset
2026-03-15T12:01:24Z upstream reset: connection refused
```
raj.s: Hmm upstream resets + ALB 5xx => could be transient conntrack or NAT gateway exhaustion between ALB and K8s nodes.
emily.g: Can we try draining one ALB target in euc1c and force traffic to other AZs as a mitigation? I can apply weighted routing to shift ~60% away from euc1c.
zach_infra: I can update weighted Route53 for ingress-api to send 60% to euc1a/euc1b (temporary). Will take ~30s to propagate.
deploy-bot: Deploy event recorded: no deploys in the last 30m for ingress-api. commit=none.
maria_ops: Customer impact: initial scan shows about 7% of total requests failing globally; errors concentrated in euc1c. Not yet hitting SLAs but some higher-traffic tenants seeing retries.
emily.g: Executing route weight change:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"ingress-api.redwood.net","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc1c","Weight":40,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"Z3...","DNSName":"alb-euc1c.amazonaws.com"}}]}}'
```
raj.s: Also increasing envoy worker threads on pods in euc1c to see if it helps. Applying k8s patch to envoy DaemonSet:
```
kubectl -n ingress-prod set env ds/envoy PROXY_WORKERS=8
```
zach_infra: Route53 change submitted. TTLs are low (10s) so shift should be visible soon. I'll also stand up an extra NLB target group with additional nodes in euc1c if we need capacity.
emily.g: After weight shift, ALB 5xx rate dropped to ~2% in 90s. Envoy reset logs reduced. CPU on nodes unchanged.
maria_ops: Notifying CS and product about degraded experience for some tenants in euc1c — brief blip, mitigation in flight. Adding incident tag to status page draft.
emily.g: I'm going to escalate to infra for a deeper postmortem and hand off to night oncall. @zach_infra can you take a follow-up to validate underlying NAT/conntrack and run packet-capture if still anomalous?
zach_infra: Taking handoff. I'll keep the weight at 40/60 until we confirm root cause and patch. Plan: collect conntrack stats, check kernel logs, test with synthetic at load.
raj.s: Queueing a runbook update: add step to adjust Route53 weights + envoy worker bump for ALB-origin 5xx spikes. Will add links to this thread.
oncall-bot: Handoff: incident owner changed from emily.g to zach_infra at 12:03 UTC. ETA for follow-up triage: 2h.
emily.g: Thanks team. Summary for the incident thread: 1) Symptom: ALB 5xx spike in euc1c driven by upstream connection resets. 2) Mitigation: shift Route53 weights, increase envoy workers. 3) Customer impact: localized failures affecting small percentage of tenants; status page updated. 4) Next steps: zach to investigate NAT/conntrack and schedule postmortem if root cause confirmed.
maria_ops: I'll attach error-rate graphs and impacted tenant list to incident tracker.
zach_infra: Acknowledged, will kick off tcpdump and conntrack dumps now and post findings in this thread. :thumbsup:
emily.g: Marking resolved in on-call channel once zach confirms stable. Great quick response everyone. :tada:
